portfolios.name: Capital Preservation Portfolio
portfolios.mandate: Park capital with near-zero drawdown in T-bills, liquid funds, and cash. Return of capital before return on capital.
portfolios.manager_bio: 18 years managing liquid and ultra-short debt funds. Prioritizes capital safety over yield, even at the cost of underperforming in rallies.

client.name: Meena Iyer
client.persona: Retired, living off savings and a small pension. Capital safety is non-negotiable, this money has to cover medical expenses, not chase returns. Checks her balance once a month, gets anxious about anything volatile.

psychographics.primary_goal: Preserve capital for medical and living costs

relationship.manager_note: Values reassurance over returns. Never lead with market volatility.

communications.summary: Monthly reassurance call, walked her through why the balance is stable despite market noise.
Called worried about a headline on markets falling, reassured, no action taken.
Sent a simple one-page monthly statement summary.

portfolios.name: Government & Corporate Bond Ladder
portfolios.mandate: Laddered exposure across GoI securities and high-grade corporate bonds for steady income with controlled duration risk.
portfolios.manager_bio: Fixed-income specialist who watches RBI policy meetings closely. Wary of duration risk if rates stay higher for longer.

client.name: Suresh Nair
client.persona: Salaried, steady 9-to-5, no time or appetite to track markets daily. Investing specifically to fund his daughter's wedding in ~3 years, wants predictable income, not surprises. Reviews his statement quarterly.

psychographics.primary_goal: Fund daughter's wedding in about 3 years

relationship.manager_note: Goal-anchored to the wedding. Keep duration short as the date nears.

communications.summary: Quarterly review email with the laddered maturity schedule ahead of the wedding.
Asked whether to lock a longer maturity, explained the duration tradeoff.
Q4 review, confirmed wedding timeline unchanged at about 3 years.

portfolios.name: Large-Cap Equity Growth Portfolio
portfolios.mandate: Core Nifty-heavyweight exposure across financials, energy, IT, and consumer names for long-term capital growth.
portfolios.manager_bio: Bullish on capex-led industrials and financials, cautious on IT services margins given global client budget pressure.

client.name: Priya Sharma
client.persona: Full-time job with a demanding schedule, investing is entirely hands-off by design. Wants a diversified, long-term core holding she can forget about for years, not something she has to actively manage alongside her career.

relationship.manager_note: Hands-off. A short WhatsApp line each quarter is enough, do not over-contact.

communications.summary: Sent the quarterly one-liner, book is up, nothing to do.
Quick thumbs-up, no questions.

portfolios.name: Banking & Financials Concentrated Portfolio
portfolios.risk_driver: Financial-sector concentration, credit cycle & NIM sensitivity
portfolios.mandate: High-conviction, concentrated bets on India's private and public banks plus leading NBFCs.
portfolios.manager_bio: Former credit analyst, deliberately concentrated. Believes India's private banks are underappreciated versus global peers.

client.name: Vikram Oberoi
client.persona: Spent 20 years in banking before retiring to angel-invest full time. Has strong, informed conviction that Indian private banks are underpriced and explicitly wants concentrated exposure, not a diversified index-hugger. Pushes back if the book gets too diluted.

relationship.manager_note: Expert and opinionated. Engage on the thesis, do not simplify.

communications.summary: Debated HDFC Bank Q1 margins, wants to stay concentrated.
Coffee meeting, reviewed the banking thesis, agreed to hold conviction.
Shared a broker note on NBFC asset quality.

portfolios.name: IT & Technology Services Portfolio
portfolios.risk_driver: Export/currency sensitivity, US & EU client discretionary IT spend
portfolios.mandate: Concentrated exposure to India's IT services exporters; returns depend heavily on US/EU enterprise tech budgets and INR/USD movement.
portfolios.manager_bio: Ex-IT-sector research analyst. Watches US mega-cap tech earnings closely, since client-budget commentary from firms like Microsoft foreshadows Indian IT services demand.

client.name: Rohan Mehta
client.persona: Deliberately invests only in what he understands, IT services, because he lives it day to day and reads every earnings call transcript for fun. Confident, opinionated, wants a research partner who can keep up, not simplify things for him.

psychographics.primary_goal: Sector-conviction growth in what he knows

relationship.manager_note: Reads every earnings call. Send primary-source detail, he will spot fluff.

communications.summary: Long email dissecting the Infosys guidance cut, wants a deep-dive on the read-through.
Sent TCS earnings-call transcript highlights.

portfolios.name: Gold & Inflation Hedge Portfolio
portfolios.mandate: Physical-gold-linked exposure via ETFs and Sovereign Gold Bonds, held as a portfolio-level inflation and currency hedge.
portfolios.manager_bio: Manages the firm's only non-equity, non-debt sleeve. Treats the gold allocation as insurance, not a return driver.

client.name: Kamala Devi
client.persona: Manages the family's wealth the way her mother did, gold has always been the trusted store of value, not an asset class to be argued about. Came to this account through her son, still prefers a phone call over an app. Deeply inflation-conscious from having lived through past rupee depreciation.

psychographics.primary_goal: Inflation protection and preserving family wealth

relationship.manager_note: Route substantive discussions through her son. Prefers phone, not app.

communications.summary: Spoke with her son, explained gold's role as an inflation hedge.
Son asked about adding to gold after the price rise, discussed.

portfolios.name: Small & Midcap Value Portfolio
portfolios.mandate: Higher-risk, higher-reward bets on midcap IT, industrials, and engineering names below the large-cap universe.
portfolios.manager_bio: Youngest PM on the desk, explicitly mandated to take more risk than the rest of the book for higher return potential.

client.name: Arjun Verma
client.persona: Dropped out of college to trade markets full time, against his family's wishes, this account is effectively his career, not a side hobby. High risk appetite by choice, checks prices multiple times a day, wants a portfolio that can compound aggressively while he's young enough to absorb the swings.

relationship.manager_note: High energy, impulsive. Reinforce position-sizing discipline every contact.

communications.summary: Asking about adding a new midcap IT name, reminded him of concentration limits.
Excited about Dixon's run, wants to increase exposure.
Flagged that smallcap volatility is elevated.

portfolios.name: Real Estate & REIT Income Portfolio
portfolios.risk_driver: Office real estate demand, rate sensitivity via yield competition
portfolios.mandate: Income-focused exposure to listed Indian REITs (office/commercial real estate) for stable distributions.
portfolios.manager_bio: Real-assets specialist. Watches commercial office leasing and vacancy trends closely, since REIT yields compete directly with bond yields.

client.name: Deepak & Ritu Kapoor
client.persona: Two demanding careers, no time to be landlords. Always liked the idea of rental income from commercial property but didn't want the hassle of actually owning and managing real estate, REITs were pitched to them as exactly that, minus the tenants and repairs.

relationship.manager_note: Want convenience and income. Lead with distributions, not price moves.

communications.summary: Quarterly distribution summary from Embassy and Mindspace REITs.
Asked about office vacancy trends, shared leasing data.

portfolios.name: Nifty 50 Index Portfolio
portfolios.risk_driver: Broad market beta, no active stock selection
portfolios.mandate: Passive, broadly diversified exposure across large-cap India equity at index-like weights. No concentrated bets, no active selection — designed to track the market, not beat it.
portfolios.manager_bio: Runs the passive sleeve. Believes most active managers don't beat the index after fees, and built this fund to prove it.

client.name: Kabir Anand
client.persona: Read enough about index investing to become mildly evangelical about it. Explicitly does not want to pay for active stock-picking he doesn't believe beats the market after fees, wants the broad India growth story, nothing more, nothing less. The most hands-off, lowest-maintenance client on the book.

relationship.manager_note: Cost-obsessed and rational. Always have expense ratio and tracking error ready.

communications.summary: Quarterly tracking-error and expense-ratio note.
Asked to confirm the fund's expense ratio versus a competitor.

portfolios.name: Balanced Advantage Hybrid Portfolio
portfolios.risk_driver: Blended equity/debt allocation, moderate volatility by design
portfolios.mandate: A single all-weather blend of large-cap equity and high-grade debt, roughly 65/35, designed so the client never has to think about rebalancing between asset classes themselves.
portfolios.manager_bio: Manages the firm's all-weather blended fund. Rebalances mechanically on a schedule, not on emotion or market calls.

client.name: Neha Kulkarni
client.persona: Runs her own store and already has enough decisions to make in a day. Explicitly asked for 'one fund that just handles the equity/debt split for me', doesn't want to be called every time the market moves, wants moderate, steady growth she can mostly ignore.

psychographics.engagement: Reviews a few times a year
psychographics.primary_goal: Steady growth with a smoother ride

relationship.manager_note: Time-poor business owner. Watch her seasonal cash needs around festivals.

communications.summary: Mid-year check-in, the balanced mix cushioned the IT drag.
Discussed cash needs for her retail business seasonality.

portfolios.name: NRI Growth Portfolio
portfolios.risk_driver: Blue-chip compounding, long time horizon, low turnover
portfolios.mandate: Long-horizon, blue-chip-only exposure for an overseas client planning an eventual return to India; prioritizes liquidity and stability over short-term alpha, mindful of eventual repatriation needs.
portfolios.manager_bio: Specializes in NRI-focused mandates. Prioritizes liquidity and blue-chip stability given clients' long-distance, lower-touch relationship with the market.

client.name: Arvind & Sunita Rao
client.occupation: NRI couple, engineers based in Dubai
client.persona: Both work in the Gulf and have been sending money home to invest for over a decade, with an eye on eventually returning to India. Communicates mostly over WhatsApp and the occasional call across time zones. Cares more about not losing money on something exotic than beating the market, wants names they'd recognize from back home.

psychographics.primary_goal: Build India-based wealth for eventual return

relationship.manager_note: Currency and repatriation-aware. Always pair reviews with an FX view.

communications.summary: Monthly review, discussed rupee levels and repatriation timing.
Asked about tax implications of an eventual return to India.

next_action.action: Monthly NRI review and FX update

portfolios.name: Retirement Income (SWP) Portfolio
portfolios.risk_driver: Dividend/income stability, sequence-of-return risk in retirement
portfolios.mandate: Income-first allocation blending dividend-paying equity, high-grade debt, and REIT distributions to support a monthly systematic withdrawal without eroding capital in a downturn.
portfolios.manager_bio: Manages income-focused retirement mandates. Obsessive about downside protection since these clients can't simply wait out a bad year.

client.name: Prakash Iyer
client.persona: Spent 35 years at a public-sector company and retired on a pension plus provident fund payout, previously kept everything in fixed deposits. Cautiously agreed to diversify a portion into this account on his relationship manager's advice, but still needs a predictable monthly withdrawal to feel comfortable, capital loss is his single biggest fear.

relationship.manager_note: Income certainty is everything. Confirm each payout, avoid surprises.

communications.summary: Confirmed the monthly SWP payout processed, income steady.
Asked whether the payout can rise with inflation, explained the annual reset.

portfolios.name: Reference Balanced 60/40 Fund
portfolios.risk_driver: N/A — fixed benchmark, not actively managed
portfolios.mandate: A fixed, broadly diversified 60% equity / 40% debt reference book computed by the exact same engine as every other fund. Exists only so any signal's impact on a real fund can be compared against what a normal, unconcentrated book would show — the 'you vs. a normal book' lens (LLD §12). Not a real desk; no active manager.
portfolios.manager_bio: N/A — fixed benchmark, not actively managed by anyone.
